entries.title: Dropping the Rifle
entries.synopsis: The Child Soldier keeps the rifle the way soldiers keep things they shouldn't. A hand-me-down maxim: the rifle kept them alive, the rifle is the only thing that did. The bunker's quiet question is who, in those quiet hours, is going to carry that misread weight away.

entries.title: First Blood at the Hatch
entries.synopsis: The Hardened Daughter eats with a piece of broken glass wrapped in cloth and watches the door. Someone will eventually have to sit beside her, in silence, until a sound outside is no longer terrifying. Then there is the day she does not flinch at it.

entries.title: Growing Up, Fast
entries.synopsis: The Naive Son draws animals on the wall and asks questions about birds. The adults answer in halves. The bunker has a list of skills and a calendar that says it is time to start teaching.

entries.title: The Pack
entries.synopsis: The Feral Orphan will not eat food that has been cooked or touched. A blanket folded and left on warm concrete stays a blanket folded on warm concrete. There is a list inside the council sheet that says: thirty days, the Vet and the Fierce Mother take turns.

entries.title: The Scavenger Alliance
entries.synopsis: A desperate faction of scavengers offers an alliance, but their loyalty is questionable.

entries.title: The Farmer's Bargain
entries.synopsis: A group of farmers offers a trade agreement for fresh food in exchange for protection.

entries.title: Mysterious Radio Signal
entries.synopsis: A strange radio signal is detected from a nearby ruin. It could be survivors... or something else.

entries.title: Medical Supply Run
entries.synopsis: A nearby settlement is in desperate need of medical supplies. Will you risk an expedition to help them?

entries.title: Black Flotilla Trade Negotiation
entries.synopsis: The notorious Black Flotilla offers a lucrative trade deal, but their reputation precedes them.

entries.title: The Half-Submerged Barrik
entries.synopsis: Coordinates and a Flotilla challenge ribbon have led you to the Half-Submerged Barrik. Inside, the remains of a pre-war crew wait in the dark. This is not a salvage run — it is a burial.

entries.title: Bunker Expansion Project
entries.synopsis: The survivors propose expanding the bunker to accommodate more people and better facilities.

entries.title: Radiation Study Expedition
entries.synopsis: Scientists from a distant settlement want to study the radiation effects in your area.

entries.title: Survivor Rescue Mission
entries.synopsis: A lone survivor is spotted injured near the perimeter. Rescue them or leave them to their fate?

entries.title: Raider Peace Offer
entries.synopsis: A raider faction offers a temporary truce in exchange for tribute.

entries.title: Expedition Equipment Upgrade
entries.synopsis: Upgrade your expedition gear to improve safety and efficiency.

entries.title: Medical Triage Decision
entries.synopsis: A critical medical emergency requires triage. Who do you save first?

entries.title: Scout Training Program
entries.synopsis: Establish a training program to improve your scouts' skills and survival rates.

entries.title: Food Storage Theft
entries.synopsis: Someone is stealing food from the bunker's storage. Investigate and stop the thief.

entries.title: Medical Experiment
entries.synopsis: A desperate medic proposes an untested medical procedure to cure radiation sickness.

entries.title: Survivor Leadership Challenge
entries.synopsis: A charismatic survivor challenges your leadership. Do you allow a vote or suppress the challenge?

entries.title: Raider Ambush
entries.synopsis: Your expedition is ambushed by raiders. Fight, flee, or negotiate?

entries.title: Bunker Defense Drill
entries.synopsis: Prepare the bunker for a potential raider attack with a defense drill.

entries.title: Survivor Memorial
entries.synopsis: Hold a memorial for the survivors who have passed away.

entries.title: Food Rationing Crisis
entries.synopsis: Food supplies are critically low. Impose rationing or risk starvation?

entries.title: Technology Scavenging Expedition
entries.synopsis: Send an expedition to scavenge for pre-war technology in a dangerous ruin.

entries.title: Medical Training Program
entries.synopsis: Establish a medical training program to improve the bunker's healthcare capabilities.

entries.title: Survivor Skills Assessment
entries.synopsis: Assess the skills of your survivors to better allocate labor and improve efficiency.

entries.title: Medical Bay Expansion
entries.synopsis: Expand the bunker's medical bay to improve healthcare capabilities.

entries.title: Survivor Romance
entries.synopsis: Two survivors have developed feelings for each other. Do you acknowledge their relationship or ignore it?

entries.title: Fuel Crisis
entries.synopsis: Fuel reserves are critically low. Do you send an expedition to scavenge or conserve what little you have?

entries.title: Eli's Pipe-Fitting Pupil
entries.synopsis: Eli was the only one who knew which elbow joint took packing and which one took thread tape. Now there is a second pair of hands that knows, and the second pair is eleven.

entries.title: Sasha's Suture Line
entries.synopsis: Sasha had the steady hands the bunker trusted with the children and the wounded. She has been teaching an apprentice how to clean and close a wound without flinching. The first closure the apprentice did alone was a small one, and it held, and the apprentice did not throw up.

entries.title: The Quiet Dial
entries.synopsis: The radio operator taught an apprentice the listening hour. The numbers station came in and the apprentice wrote it down without being told, on the second try, while the rest of the bunker slept. The dial is not a skill. The dial is a habit.

entries.title: The Furnace Daughter
entries.synopsis: She was always the one who fed the forge. The apprentice learned the rhythm last winter: when the coke is right, when the slag breaks, when the billet is ready and when it is not. The first time she pulled an ingot alone with the master watching, no one clapped. They said nothing, which was the right thing to say.

entries.title: The Hatch Watcher
entries.synopsis: A child took the hatch watch alone for ninety minutes for the first time and the click of the counter was the only sound in the whole bunker for those ninety minutes. The master watched from inside. The watcher's hands were not shaking by minute forty-five.

entries.title: Adaeze's Triage Understudy
entries.synopsis: The triage line at 03:00 is the one the bunker runs once a week so the new ones can practice. The first solo triaged patient was not a real patient but the apprentice had to walk through the steps as if she were. The steps held up.

entries.title: The Reading Hour
entries.synopsis: The bunker's only alphabet chart lives on a wall in the cold room. The children have to learn to read because the only books left are the ones the adults are willing to speak aloud. The Reading Hour is one hour a day and the children are willing. The Mechanical Hour is a different hour, and they are willing for that one too.

entries.title: The Mechanical Hour
entries.synopsis: The Mechanical Hour starts after the Reading Hour, in the same room, at the same lamp. The children learn which valve does what, and why the pumps sound the way they do when the outflow constipates. The teacher is the same person who taught the last cohort.

entries.title: First Stitches
entries.synopsis: A child hands the needle, a child hands the thread, and eventually a child closes the first wound she was not the one to make. The teacher is the bunker's only field medic and the class is small and the classroom is the infirmary floor.

entries.title: The Burned-Out Rifle
entries.synopsis: There is a rifle with no ammunition, in the storeroom, on a shelf, that the children are taught to disassemble and reassemble in the dark. The first time the disassembled rifle fell back together in the dark, the child did not flinch. Some of the adults were not sure that was a good thing.

entries.title: The Quiet Adoption
entries.synopsis: A casualty orphan from the winter convoy was folded into the bunker's census without ceremony. The adults who raised the child were not the biological parents of any child. They learned to share a cot and a ration, and they did, because the calendar said the convoy was not coming back.

entries.title: The Fierce Mother's House
entries.synopsis: The Feral Orphan was assigned a rotation with the Fierce Mother and the Vet, on the council sheet, in plain ink. The Fierce Mother sleeps with one hand on the dog. The Vet sleeps with one hand on the knife. The Orphan slept, finally, with one hand on nothing. That was the small victory.

entries.title: A Hundred and Fourteen
entries.synopsis: A casualty orphan was assigned, by plot number, to a farmer couple who still held the allotment waiting list from before. The plot was 114. It was a plum number on the list. The adults said the plum number killed the convoy that carried the child's old family and were immediately sorry for saying so.

entries.title: The Children of the Archive
entries.synopsis: The municipal archive adopted four orphans when the bunker census crossed the binder threshold for the first time. The newest intake was logged under the next four open plot numbers. The older children carried the binders to the new shelf before the new children learned which shelf it was.

entries.title: The First Surface Trip
entries.synopsis: The bunker's hatch opened the morning of day ninety-four with a child on the perimeter walk, in clean clothes, with the hatch lead close enough to catch the child's silhouette if the silhouette needed catching. The child walked one hundred metres into the scrub and did not turn around. By minute four, the child had stopped looking up.

entries.title: The First Solo Watch
entries.synopsis: Solo watch starts at minute zero and ends when the clock says it ends. The first time a child took the post alone, the Geiger counter was quiet, nothing came in over the radio, and the hatch did not move. The watch was not heroic. The watch was the watch.

entries.title: The Relay Count Cipher
entries.synopsis: An eerie five-figure shortwave broadcast loops on 104.5 MHz. Decrypting the coordinates requires Communications Codebook Alpha excavated from the Collapsed Command Vault to unlock Hidden Relay Bunker 09.

entries.title: Winter Ledger Decryption
entries.synopsis: Automated logistics transmissions report cold-storage inventory offsets. A laminated cipher sheet reveals the Sub-Basement Logistics Reserve.

entries.title: Last Rotation Dead-Hand
entries.synopsis: A military dead-hand standby broadcast prompts for authentication at Waypoint November. Microfilm index cylinder decodes the Dead-Drop Command Shelter coordinates.

entries.title: Waystation A: Soot Filter Flush
entries.synopsis: Warden Kessel reports severe coal dust clogging the primary ventilation intake at Waystation A in the Cut. Deliver clean water and filter membrane to restore air cycling.

entries.title: Switchback Waystation: Scree Shoring
entries.synopsis: Recent rockslides threaten to sweep the lower bunkhouse off the cliff ledge at the Switchback Waystation. Transport structural timbers and scrap metal to reinforce the cribbing.

entries.title: Span 44: Railway Abutment Repair
entries.synopsis: Foreman Taggart requires mechanical fasteners and welding electrodes to secure the settling western bridge pier on Railway Span 44 before heavy iron convoys can cross.

entries.title: Verity Motel: Deep Well Desilt
entries.synopsis: Fine sand and silt have jammed the deep-aquifer impeller at the Verity Motel staging post. Clean the manifold and replace the drive belt to restore potable water dispensing.

entries.title: Lock Gate Four: Sluice Valve Reclaim
entries.synopsis: Heavy brine scale has frozen the tidal sluice bypass at Lock Gate Four. Apply anti-corrosive solvent and grease to re-open the maritime staging basin.

entries.title: Verge Silo: Sentry Ration Accord
entries.synopsis: Central Garrison sentries are demanding excess grain tithes at the Verge Silo Waystation. Negotiate a standardized tariff or provide emergency rations to prevent an embargo.

entries.title: Rescue: Trapped Mechanic
entries.synopsis: A distress signal on 88.3 MHz reports a mechanic trapped at the rail depot. Her leg is pinned under a beam. She has water for two more days.

entries.title: Rescue: Injured Trader
entries.synopsis: A distress signal on 156.8 MHz reports an injured trader on Route 6. He has trade goods to share if rescued.

entries.title: Rescue: Family Shelter
entries.synopsis: A child's voice on 445.2 MHz reports her mother is sick and unresponsive. The bunker has a blue door and a broken lock.

entries.title: Investigation: Raider Lure
entries.synopsis: A suspicious signal on 192.4 MHz mentions an unguarded fuel cache. The signal pattern is too consistent to be genuine.
entries.warningText: This is a raider trap. Responding will trigger an ambush.

entries.title: Rescue: Stranded Military Patrol
entries.synopsis: A military distress signal on 901.2 MHz reports Sergeant Voss's patrol six pinned down with two wounded. Ammunition low.

entries.title: The Water Station Route
entries.synopsis: A caravan factor working the water stations is short after a bad crossing. What you do about it is the first entry in her ledger.

entries.title: Wreckage on the Cut Road
entries.synopsis: The caravan factor's second wagon is through the road crust, and she is camped on the wreck guarding the cargo.

entries.title: The Coordinator's Stamp
entries.synopsis: The grain exchange has given Mara Veln the southern routes. The rate sheet has a line for friends of the coordinator.

entries.title: Eight Beds
entries.synopsis: An almshouse clinic is down to its last shelves; its physician shows the inventory before asking for anything.

entries.title: The Fever Finds the Almshouse
entries.synopsis: The clinic is full of a fever she can name but not stop, and the camp is one rumor from a cordon.

entries.title: The Door That Stays Open
entries.synopsis: The clinic trains more hands than it loses now; the verge sends its sick to a door never shut at the appointed hour.

entries.title: Checkpoint Gamma
entries.synopsis: A garrison checkpoint runs by the book, and the corporal keeps the book where petitioners can read it.

entries.title: The Margin Notes
entries.synopsis: The corporal who wrote dated objections to his own orders is now the subject of them.

entries.title: Word Before the Sweeps
entries.synopsis: An outside ally sends warning before every sweep: routes, timing, the mood of the command.

entries.title: The Girl Who Counts
entries.synopsis: A child keeps order in a queue at the baths, and her count is better than yours.

entries.title: Lessons Twice Given
entries.synopsis: The shelter's foundling sits the lessons it gives and invents the ones it will not.

entries.title: Small Hands, Steady Ones
entries.synopsis: The counting becomes a trade instead of a defense: medic's apprentice, roster, and all.

entries.title: Live Grounds, No Copper
entries.synopsis: A grid engineer holds a live substation with working grounds and no copper to speak of.

entries.title: One Feeder at a Time
entries.synopsis: A regional recovery project wants her name on it and her switching orders behind it.

entries.title: The Region On Schedule
entries.synopsis: The grid is small, documented, and true: two feeders, a schedule, and switching orders done safely.

entries.title: The Hours of the Camp
entries.synopsis: A refugee camp keeps its hours, and raiders have begun keeping watch on it.

entries.title: The Rota and the Schism
entries.synopsis: The camps quarrel over the right way to keep the hours, and both sides quote her.

entries.title: The Verdict-Free Hour
entries.synopsis: When the camps quarrel, they send for her before they send for anyone with a rifle.

entries.title: The Real Floors
entries.synopsis: A scavenger knows which cellar floors are real, and offers to split a find rather than race.

entries.title: A Rumor With a Drop Shaft
entries.synopsis: A cellar floor that was a rumor took her ankle, and she is camp-bound with a registry full of addresses.

entries.title: First Refusal
entries.synopsis: The guild gave her the cellar registry, and the registry has your name in the margin.

entries.title: The Station That Answers
entries.synopsis: A relay mast lives on scavenged cells and inherited discipline, and its operator answers on schedule.

entries.title: Somebody Maps the Towers
entries.synopsis: The faction that maps towers has mapped hers, and their survey team is two valleys out.

entries.title: Fixed Hours
entries.synopsis: A station that answers on schedule, under a flag that leaves it alone, with a band of its own.

entries.title: The Settled Figure
entries.synopsis: Half a wagon and a whole debt, both priced daily. The buyout figure exists and is written down. The only question is whose hand moves first: yours to help him r

entries.title: Rounding for the Living
entries.synopsis: The overflow clinic's stock does not reconcile with the garrison's ledgers, and the difference keeps matching a list of people who are alive anyway. The audit i

entries.title: Staffing the Schedule
entries.synopsis: The batching plant restart is real, the schedule is honest, and the schedule does not care what happened to the night shift. He needs crews who pass the checkli

entries.title: What I Have Walked
entries.synopsis: The route scavenger sells only what he has walked, and the best route in the roll is the one he learned the impolite way. The copy costs less than the question

entries.title: Two Versions
entries.synopsis: The bridge corridor's crossing log is kept in full view, and the incident reports come back in two versions: what she filed and what command acknowledges. She w

entries.title: A Year That Has Not Happened
entries.synopsis: The seed annex holds tested lots and one roof of uncertain honesty. She will not leave it and she will not hurry it, and the private tin is not for discussion.

entries.title: The Fine Herd
entries.synopsis: The herd ledger and the herd disagree by exactly the animals a hard winter eats, and the well has been dosed since before anyone asked. What the herd needs is a

entries.title: The Honest Notebooks
entries.synopsis: Four notebooks of repeats, every published solution refuted in writing including his own, and a standing rule that patrons get warned before they get taken. Fun

entries.title: What the Manifest Says
entries.synopsis: The field kitchen's pot is honest and the manifest is not, and she is the difference. The portion ledger disagrees with the pot by exactly the amount the childr

entries.title: Which Kind of Cook
entries.synopsis: The store mess runs institutional-exact under a cook with one private crate of good oil and an argument with himself that has been going since autumn. The crate

entries.title: Posted Odds
entries.synopsis: The wagon mechanic keeps one vehicle alive past decency and tells you the odds on every road like a man reading weather. The bearing in his toolbox has a story

entries.title: The Private Log
entries.synopsis: The generator runs to stated hours and the private log runs to stated truth: a missed maintenance interval in her own handwriting, kept so somebody remembers wh

entries.title: Walk With Me at Dawn
entries.synopsis: The old hunting lines fed the settlement for two winters and have stopped feeding it, and the hunter will hear no word against them before dawn. At dawn, the ro

entries.title: Marked Paths
entries.synopsis: The trap circuit is marked, posted, and paid for, once, in the way that taught her. The standing fee for the maimed still stands. The fog month is a closed subj

entries.title: The Page on the Desk
entries.synopsis: The archive's copy lessons are exact and one page of the community record is in a different hand than the rest. It sits face-up on the desk through every lesson

entries.title: The Rest of the Map
entries.synopsis: The runner knows the corridors grown-ups cannot stand up in, and has decided your column watches. The routes have never been written down, because paper can be
